findings.claim: The development-selected early-curvature projection provides a robust predictive improvement over matched controls on previously withheld doses.
findings.falsification: On reserved doses, all three named controls beat the selected equation.
findings.known_prior_art: PET-quenching relief under phosphorylation and Michaelis-Menten initial velocities are reported by the authors. Our late-curve calibrated forecast is separate; neither first-order saturation nor power laws are novel families.
findings.negative_evidence_disposition: supported: this proposed improvement is falsified by the reserved-dose comparison

findings.claim: Same-curve early response carries useful later-response information; carrying F6 unchanged is much less accurate than its calibrated tangent on these two doses.
findings.falsification: A useful calibration control is not a novel kinetic law; only two doses, no biological replicate identification.
findings.known_prior_art: PET-quenching relief under phosphorylation and Michaelis-Menten initial velocities are reported by the authors. Our late-curve calibrated forecast is separate; neither first-order saturation nor power laws are novel families.

findings.claim: The inverse-dose saturation parameterization cannot be interpreted as identified substrate depletion.
findings.falsification: Unconstrained exponent reaches its preset boundary; enforcing nondecreasing substrate-pool timescale does not beat development controls.
findings.scope: Falsifies this fitted explanation, not all biochemical depletion mechanisms.
findings.known_prior_art: PET-quenching relief under phosphorylation and Michaelis-Menten initial velocities are reported by the authors. Our late-curve calibrated forecast is separate; neither first-order saturation nor power laws are novel families.
findings.underlying_proposal_disposition: unsupported: inverse-dose fit does not identify substrate depletion
